title.value: Definitive Care for Severely Injured Children in Quebec
title.justification: The title 'Definitive Care for Severely Injured Children in Quebec' reflects the paper's focus, which is on improving trauma care for children in Quebec, particularly in indigenous and remote areas.
title.quote: Definitive Care for Severely Injured Children in Quebec

extractions.description: This paper analyzes trauma care outcomes for severely injured children in various regions of Quebec, focusing on disparities in care access and outcomes for Indigenous and Northern Quebec communities. The study found longer hospital stays for patients from Northern Quebec and highlights the need for improved trauma systems and regional care to reduce inequities.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The central theme of this paper is healthcare delivery and outcomes for pediatric trauma patients in Quebec, rather than Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Conclusion: ICU admission rate was similar among Northern and off-island populations. Patients from Northern Quebec appeared to have longer-than-median hospital length of stay.

primary_category.quote: Injury is the leading cause of death in children over the age of one in Canada, and remains the most common cause of death in Quebec pediatric patients.
